title: Insomniac回应金刚狼气味轨迹争议
text:
相关文章: 《漫威金刚狼》游戏评测｜IGN 中国
围绕PS5独占游戏《漫威金刚狼》中的「气味轨迹」机制，近日玩家间出现了一场关于「屁气」的争论。部分玩家希望开发商Insomniac Games加入关闭选项，不过官方表示，这一效果并不会在游戏中一直显示。
《漫威金刚狼》中，罗根在特定情况下可以看到气味轨迹，并借此追踪人物或线索。这项机制其实早在今年夏季便已公开，但随着本周游戏评测陆续上线，相关讨论再次升温。 还有更多相关内容 《漫威金刚狼》真人宣传视频
《华盛顿邮报》记者Gene Park将这种视觉效果戏称为「屁气」，原因是罗根追踪其他角色时，气味轨迹会出现在人物身后。他还指出，即使关闭部分辅助和导航选项，这些气味轨迹仍然存在。部分玩家一度认为，该效果可以通过无障碍设置关闭。《漫威金刚狼》的官方无障碍功能中确实包含「追逐辅助」选项，可以在追逐环节降低目标的移动速度，但这一功能并不会关闭气味轨迹。其他导航相关选项同样无法将其移除。
因此，一些玩家认为气味轨迹在游戏中会始终开启，并呼吁Insomniac加入关闭功能。对此，Insomniac社区及市场总监James Stevenson在社交媒体上作出澄清。他表示：「气味轨迹并不是一直开启的。它代表了罗根在原作设定中拥有的变种人超级感官和顶尖追踪能力。只有在他追踪某种特定气味或声音时才会出现，比如某个人、威士忌或其他线索。这通常出现在剧情、任务环节，或者当他察觉到附近存在收集品时。」
不过，即便如此，仍有玩家希望游戏能够彻底关闭这种被戏称为「屁气」的视觉提示。相关批评主要认为，气味轨迹对玩家的引导过于直接。有人援引之前关于《最终幻想》系列黄色油漆引导线的讨论 ，指出这些引导线消除了追逐战或探索等环节所需的任何技巧。
这也进一步引出了一个问题：如何把金刚狼本身的能力合理转化成游戏机制。按照原作设定，拥有超强感官的罗根理论上不会花费大量时间在场景中漫无目的地寻找目标，甚至寻找下一瓶酒。但如果完全按照这一设定设计，游戏中的探索过程又可能因此失去挑战。
部分玩家因此建议，可以把气味追踪设计成由玩家主动触发的能力，例如按下DualSense手柄的R3键后才显示轨迹，让不希望依赖提示的玩家自行选择是否使用。不过从Stevenson的回应来看，Insomniac似乎认为这种设计并不符合罗根的角色设定。Stevenson随后还进一步解释，在寻找隐藏收集品时，玩家必须先探索到距离目标足够近的位置，罗根才能听到声音或闻到气味。因此，玩家仍然需要自行探索地图，气味轨迹并不会直接从远处标出所有收集品的位置。
相关文章: 《漫威金刚狼》宣传视频

title: 《雷顿教授》开发商回应游戏使用生成式AI
text:
相关文章: 《雷顿教授与蒸汽新世界》发售日预告 | 任天堂直面会
在粉丝发现《雷顿教授与不可思议的小镇 重制版》《DECAPOLICE》等游戏的宣传片中存在「AI垃圾」后，开发商Level-5就使用生成式AI一事道歉并作出解释。
相关担忧出现在本周早些时候Level-5举行的一场类似任天堂直面会的发布会之后。这场名为「Level5 Vision 2026 II: Dreams」的发布会首次展示了多款即将推出的游戏，同时也出现了多处被粉丝怀疑使用生成式AI的内容。
半路失去台阶的楼梯
观看这场50分钟发布会的观众，花在讨论疑似使用AI证据上的时间，甚至比讨论游戏本身还多，其中涉及《雷顿教授》重制版、《妖怪手表2 霸道》和《DECAPOLICE》等作品。引发争议的画面大多只出现在背景场景中，但真正让事情演变成这家日本工作室全面争议的，是粉丝不得不首先去质疑Level-5是否使用了AI这件事本身。
一名粉丝在X/Twitter上表示：「Level-5宣布将凭借《雷顿教授》《DECAPOLICE》《妖怪手表》等作品大举回归时，我真的特别兴奋。但看到他们在这么多游戏里如此明目张胆地使用生成式AI……对，这真的不行。」另一名粉丝表示：「你们曾经是一家很棒的工作室。现在你们带给我们的只有失望。我们不想要这种AI垃圾。」
Level-5社长兼CEO日野晃博也通过X回应争议。此前他还以自己的动画形象主持了这场发布会。他发布的内容既是一份道歉，也是一番解释，并确认Level-5确实在部分开发环节中使用了生成式AI。
日野晃博将Level-5大量使用AI形容为「对最新技术的实验」，并补充表示，团队「对于任何因此感到不适的人，诚挚致歉」。
日野晃博表示：「不过，请大家放心，我们已经发售作品中所有决定其魅力与个性的要素——例如剧本、角色设计以及基础设定——全部都是由人类亲手创作的。我们主要利用AI来提高将人工创作素材数字化的效率，例如把原画准确转换成3D多边形模型。大家可以放心，我们推出的游戏中不存在单纯由AI生成的内容。」
日野晃博还为Level-5目前使用AI的方式进行了辩护。他表示：「通过AI提高效率节省下来的时间，让我们的创作者能够把更多精力投入到真正的创作本质之中。」在他和团队看来，《雷顿教授与不可思议的小镇》等游戏的最终版本依然会让粉丝满意。Level-5此次如此大量采用生成式AI的部分原因，是希望把「大型作品目前长达5年的开发周期缩短至2年」。
他继续表示：「话虽如此，我们不能否认，这一次确实大量使用了AI，因为我们希望呈现出一场视觉效果突出、同时又容易理解的发布会。我们会把这次经历当作未来的一次学习机会，也请大家期待Level-5下一次的发布会。」
不过，这番解释并没有得到社区的良好回应。在这条帖子的回复中，仍有粉丝对生成式技术被用于任何开发环节感到担忧，并害怕受到影响的游戏会因此永远留下污点。一条获得较多关注的回复表示：「生成式AI是科技公司利用无数艺术家被盗用的作品训练出来的，他们借这些艺术家的作品获利，目的就是取代艺术家。你们使用这种技术，也就意味着你们取代了艺术家。你们正在依靠那些作品被盗、用来驱动这类软件的艺术家的技能赚钱。」
对于Level-5今后将如何调整开发计划，日野晃博并没有公布具体方案。目前，作为2007年原版游戏重制作品的《雷顿教授与不可思议的小镇 重制版》计划于2027年登陆PC和主机平台。系列另一款全新作品《雷顿教授与蒸汽新世界》则计划于今年12月发售。

title: 印达·纳瓦雷特已有计划练好罗刹女的南方口音
text:
相关文章: 阿萨·格尔曼加盟新版《X战警》，饰演天使
凭借《痴迷》崭露头角的印达·纳瓦雷特已经有了自己的计划，确保能在新版《X战警》电影中准确演绎罗刹女标志性的美国南方口音。
纳瓦雷特将在2028年从恐怖片领域跨入MCU，出演《X战警》。正如上个月公布的消息，该片定于2028年5月5日上映。不过，相比罗刹女吸收他人能力的超能力以及强势的性格，粉丝们更想知道的是，纳瓦雷特是否会为罗刹女的声音带来那种独特的南方韵味。
这个角色一直以浓重的南方口音闻名，尤其是得益于原版《X战警》动画剧集配音演员莉诺·赞（Lenore Zann）广受欢迎的演绎。纳瓦雷特本人或许并没有观众印象中罗刹女应有的天然口音，但她告诉《今晚娱乐》，自己已经在认真考虑这名变种人成员应该拥有怎样的声音。
当被问到会如何塑造罗刹女的声音时，纳瓦雷特表示：「这件事我以前从没公开说过——我自己都完全忘了——我来自一个父母离异的家庭。我人生中很长一段时间都是在得州长大的。所以说实话，我真的特别喜欢那些南方女性。」
随后，纳瓦雷特特别提到了自己与科珀斯克里斯蒂的联系。这是一座位于得州南部沿海地区的城市。对于这位从《痴迷》演员变身漫威超级英雄的演员来说，她「真的、真的很喜欢」那些「上了年纪的南方女性」。不过，她对美国南方的喜爱还不止于此。她继续说道：「但尤其是密西西比州——罗刹女就来自密西西比州。所以我真的很想亲自去那里。我希望能够真正演好她，不辜负这个角色。」 还有更多相关内容 《X战警》重启作品将从漫画中寻求灵感
在《X战警》正式上映之前，还有许多环节需要落实，不过导演杰克·施莱尔已经暗示，这会是一部值得等待的团队电影。今年8月，他谈到了自己正在参考的一些漫画作品，并承诺会为MCU粉丝带来一部与此前真人版《X战警》电影相比具有「全新演绎」的作品。与此同时，据报道，纳瓦雷特对于参演这部电影非常兴奋，甚至因此放弃了出演《盗火线2》的机会。
相关文章: 《X战警》重启阵容公布：金刚狼、万磁王缺席

title: 开发者称没必要推出《魔兽世界2》
text:
相关文章: 《魔兽世界：无限》公布预告
《魔兽世界：无限》开发者Kris Zierhut和Mike Nuthals详细介绍了游戏的新功能，并解释了为什么他们认为没有必要推出《魔兽世界2》。 还有更多相关内容 《魔兽世界：至暗之夜》评测
《魔兽世界：无限》是这一长寿系列的「经典+」版本，让玩家能够回到经过更新的原版艾泽拉斯，其中将加入新的区域、地下城、团队副本等内容。该作于昨天的暴雪嘉年华2026开幕式上正式公布。如今，游戏开发者进一步解释了为什么他们认为，这种对经典版本的全新演绎——再加上周末公布的其他多项《魔兽世界》更新——已经让长期传闻中的《魔兽世界2》变得没有必要。
Zierhut表示：「我认为，《魔兽世界》最独特、最了不起的一点就在于，我们拥有这样一款游戏、这样一个世界，以及这样一套设计，而且过去25年里一直都在持续开发。我们一直在让它变得更好。我们提升了画面，改进了渲染，改善了光照效果；还有今天在舞台上展示的所有那些新东西。与此同时，我们也让引擎绘制和移动内容的方式变得更加高效。服务器的运行方式、处理玩家以及让玩家在世界中移动的方式，还有所有负责法术和战斗的系统，这些年来全都变得更加高效、更好了。我们现在拥有一套非常出色的游戏引擎和服务器基础设施，可以说无人能及。为什么要把这些全部丢掉，然后从头开始？」
Zierhut接着表示，除了《魔兽世界：无限》在技术层面的进步之外，团队依然希望继续构建当前《魔兽世界》宇宙的故事。Zierhut说：「这并不是说现在的故事有什么问题。我们喜欢这个故事。所以回到最初的时代，通过《魔兽世界：无限》，我们就有机会用全新、不同的方式探索这些故事。因此《魔兽世界2》带不来什么《魔兽世界：无限》现在还没有提供的。」
正如昨天舞台上公布的那样，《魔兽世界：无限》并不只是对原版游戏简单翻新。除了「经过更新的世界画面与光照」外，游戏还将加入10人和20人团队副本、超过1000个全新任务、新的种族与职业组合、新种族Skyborne等内容。Nuthals和Zierhut表示，其中有几项关键功能是他们最期待玩家亲自体验的。
Nuthals表示：「我特别期待玩家发现我们所有的新物品。所有地下城和团队副本的物品配置都经过了重新调整。有太多新东西可以探索。我真的很期待玩家进入游戏、探索整个世界，发现各种有趣的角落，找到那些很棒的战利品，然后好好享受游戏。至于团队副本，我觉得自己最期待的是副本人数规模。我们会有兽穴深渊，这是一个10人团队副本；还会有20人的海加尔山之巅，而奥妮克希亚则会是40人副本。我觉得最让我兴奋的，是让玩家去找到社交圈和朋友，然后把这些队伍组起来。」
Zierhut表示：「我最期待的是露营功能。大家可能还记得，以前在《魔兽世界》里，你可以放下一个烹饪用的篝火，然后坐在那里做饭。现在，这种烹饪篝火变成了基础营火。而当你坐在那里等待时——因为你需要在那里待上一分钟——可能会有另一名玩家路过，然后他也加入进来。于是你们都待在那里，要一起等一分钟，你可能就会说：『嘿，你在做什么任务？哦，我们做的是同一个任务。要不一起组队吧？』而这正是友谊、人际关系以及公会诞生的时刻。我真的很期待这个功能会给我们的游戏带来什么。」
虽然《魔兽世界：无限》会加入大量新内容供玩家探索，但Zierhut和Nuthals表示，它不会偏离玩家喜爱的原版体验太远。Zierhut表示：「我们不会对背景设定作出大幅修改。我们不会改变这个世界给人的感觉，但我们或许可以稍微调整一些事件发生的顺序。这不会与经典版中的内容产生矛盾，只是会稍微有所不同。因此，我们有空间去讲述一个略有不同的故事。大家不必担心时间线会出现问题。」Nuthals表示：「我们的核心支柱非常普遍，也始终是游玩经典版《魔兽世界》体验的核心。这一直都是我们在脑海中考虑的事情。想到玩家真正进入游戏并开始游玩之后会做些什么，就让人非常兴奋。」
《魔兽世界：无限》将于11月4日推出。
相关文章: 暴雪嘉年华 2026 将于 9 月回归

title: 《守望先锋》开发者确认猎空仍是游戏吉祥物
text:
相关文章: 《守望先锋》「血律」角色预告
各位，这下可以确定了：尽管猎空最近并没有频繁出现在大型联动或宣传素材中，但她依然是《守望先锋》的门面角色。
在2026年暴雪嘉年华期间，我们有机会与《守望先锋》的开发团队坐下来交流，讨论了游戏最新的支援英雄血律、系列未来的发展方向，同时也追问了猎空作为所谓游戏吉祥物的地位。
我们直接询问了《守望先锋》首席英雄制作人Kenny Hudson以及艺术总监Dion Rogers：猎空现在是否仍然是这款游戏的吉祥物——或者说，她过去是否真的被团队视为吉祥物。
他们的回答明确而坚定：猎空现在是、而且一直都是《守望先锋》的吉祥物。Rogers告诉我们：「猎空仍然是《守望先锋》的吉祥物。毫无疑问。『猎空橙』是团队一直都会说的一个词。守望先锋标志顶部的那一部分也是橙色。她依然是那个女孩。」 还有更多相关内容 《守望先锋》「釜山群英」赛季预告
《守望先锋》刚刚推出了全新的支援英雄血律，这是一名以吸血鬼为灵感、并且与末日铁拳有着深厚渊源的角色。不，他并不是真正的吸血鬼，但Rogers表示，这一主题从最初开始就是角色设计的重要组成部分。他解释道：「这个想法来自我们的首席叙事设计师Miranda Moyer，她当时提出了一个问题：『如果《守望先锋》宇宙里有吸血鬼，他会是什么样子？』当我们能够围绕一个非常酷的主题进行创作时，往往最能做出优秀的英雄，而『吸血鬼』这个概念立刻让大家在技能组、概念和美术等各方面都有了很多灵感。」
Hudson补充道：「这个角色做起来很有意思，因为到了第54号英雄，我们已经做过牛仔、骑士、忍者这些各种典型角色了。当我们想到吸血鬼时，就觉得：『对，就顺着这个方向继续做，看看能不能把它变成一个英雄。』他本质上依然是一名科学家或者机械工程师，就连他的披风看起来也依然有点像实验服，保留了他身上的科学家元素……最开始，我们把他设计成一名科学家，一个很普通的人，穿实验服、戴眼镜。有时候，一个角色需要团队在看到某张图时直接说出：『这就是那个英雄。』但当时他还没有完全达到这种感觉。不过我们加入了Miranda提到的吸血鬼元素之后，他才真正开始像一个英雄了。你能看到明确的主题、幻想感以及角色原型。我们让他来自非洲津巴布韦，也立即赋予了他相应的文化背景，以及与末日铁拳之间的联系。他人生中的某个阶段曾为末日铁拳的家族工作，还帮助末日铁拳打造过手臂，所以后来他去找末日铁拳，想把自己的手臂重新拿回来，这样也就说得通了。」
血律几乎是今年加入《守望先锋》的10名角色中的最后一位。2026年游戏推出了如此大量的新内容，我们也不得不问，《守望先锋》接下来还有哪些高峰可以挑战，团队又在准备些什么。
Rogers表示：「永远都有空间加入更多英雄。我们还在准备很多东西。」Hudson补充道：「重点并不是再次达到那些我们已经实现过的目标，而是设定新的目标，看看我们还能把游戏带到什么地方。过去几年里，整个团队学到了很多东西，我们非常期待利用这些经验真正把自己推向新的领域，以全新、有趣的方式继续进化。」

title: 《暗黑破坏神》开发者对Netflix动画剧集感到非常兴奋
text:
相关文章: 《暗黑破坏神4》「地狱遗赠」赛季预告
《暗黑破坏神4》的主要开发者谈到了他们对全新《暗黑破坏神》Netflix动画剧集、游戏Switch 2版本以及「地狱遗赠」赛季的期待。
在昨天暴雪嘉年华开幕式公布的众多消息中，《暗黑破坏神》将推出Netflix剧集这件事，至少已经让该系列其中一支开发团队迫不及待。昨天，暴雪总裁Johanna Faries透露，一部《暗黑破坏神》动画剧集正在制作中，但她也承认，目前还「不能透露太多」，暂时无法说明这部新剧具体会讲些什么。
尽管如此，《暗黑破坏神4》的开发团队表示，这很可能是他们最兴奋的一项公布，甚至超过了《暗黑破坏神5》将于2029年推出、《暗黑破坏神4》将登陆Switch 2、再生侠将加入《暗黑破坏神：不朽》，以及亚马逊职业登场等消息。昨天消息公布后，IGN与《暗黑破坏神4》游戏总监Brent Gibson，以及《暗黑破坏神4：地狱遗赠》赛季负责人Owen Leach进行了交流，详细聊了这些内容。
Gibson表示：「虽然我完全没有相关信息，也不能分享任何东西，但我们要有自己的剧集了，这就是最让我兴奋的事情。我是个喜欢故事的人。我想看到更多故事，故事当然是越多越好。我们现在正在逐步确定这部剧的创作团队，也正在实现Johanna所说的那句话：我们是Blizzard Entertainment。我认为《暗黑破坏神》的世界非常适合作为讲述这些故事的起点，所以我们能拥有一部自己的剧集，我真的高兴得不能再高兴了。」
在昨天的发布会上，Faries还提到，《守望先锋》《魔兽争霸》以及「或许还有一些……其他（暴雪）宇宙」未来也可能推出各自的剧集。不过至少目前，仅仅是《暗黑破坏神》将被改编成剧集的消息，就已经足以让开发团队持续兴奋。 还有更多相关内容 《暗黑破坏神4》「地狱遗赠」赛季实机演示
Leach表示：「如果以一个粉丝的身份回答，最让我兴奋的就是这部剧。我看过Netflix上的动画剧集，然后我的反应就是：超级兴奋！」Gibson补充道：「我觉得，现在这些IP存在于多种不同媒体中的世界，就像是一片蛮荒之地。你根本没办法预测这些机制最终会如何运作。你可以看看其他那些推出过剧集的游戏，以及这些剧集如何进一步提升并改变了它们。《辐射》就是一个非常好的例子。你能看到，因为剧集的推出，游戏迎来了一次巨大的复兴，我很喜欢这种现象。我完全不知道它最后会走向哪里，但现在正是合适的时机，我对此非常兴奋。」
除了全新的Netflix剧集外，Gibson和Leach表示，《暗黑破坏神》宇宙还有很多值得玩家期待的内容。Leach表示：「作为『地狱遗赠』赛季的负责人，我真的非常兴奋，因为迪亚波罗终于要出现在《暗黑破坏神4》里了。我简直要疯了，而且这还只是其中一个Boss。我们一共有20个全新Boss。还有来自《暗黑破坏神：地狱火》的Na-Krul。我相信现场观众知道这件事之后一定会疯掉。所以9月15日，我真的等不及了。我非常期待玩家和我们一起庆祝系列30周年。」
Gibson表示，他同样很期待玩家能够在9月15日于Switch 2上玩到《暗黑破坏神4》。Gibson表示：「早就该来了。从第一天开始，我们就一直在讨论登陆掌机平台意味着什么。我真的被他们最终做到的品质水平震撼到了。那里有一批我们此前一直没有服务到的玩家。我记得它好像曾经出现在大家最希望Switch 2首发就能拥有的十大游戏名单里。而我的想法就是：『对，我也是这么想的。现在终于来了。』所以我非常高兴。」
Leach补充道：「我喜欢那种可以随时随地游玩的灵活性。我以前会在Steam Deck上玩，但如果能有一个专门针对这台主机打造的版本，那就更好了。所以现在我懒的时候就在沙发上玩，有些时候则会在PC上玩。我们就是这么玩的。」

title: 杰洛特皮肤将登陆《暗黑破坏神4》
text:
相关文章: 《暗黑破坏神4》「地狱遗赠」赛季预告
CD Projekt和暴雪首次公开了《暗黑破坏神4》野蛮人的杰洛特主题皮肤，不过想要获得这款皮肤，你需要在战网预购《巫师3：狂猎》资料片《旧时曲》。 还有更多相关内容 《暗黑破坏神4》「地狱遗赠」赛季实机演示
在2026年暴雪嘉年华期间，CD Projekt高级社区与社交媒体经理Amelia Korzycka和关卡设计负责人Miles Tost作为嘉宾参加了「战网30周年」座谈会，并在现场公开了这款皮肤。战网玩家只要提前购买《旧时曲》——目前该资料片还只能加入愿望单——或在资料片发售后购买，就可以获得这款皮肤。这意味着杰洛特皮肤被限定在战网平台，也就是说，例如Steam玩家就无法获得。
可以想象，这项安排并没有得到那些已经在非战网平台拥有《巫师3：狂猎》的《暗黑破坏神4》玩家欢迎。《巫师3》重制版将于2026年9月29日登陆Steam，所有已经拥有游戏本体的玩家都可以免费升级。因此，那些已经在Steam上拥有《巫师3：狂猎》的玩家——到了现在，还有谁没有呢？——如果对《旧时曲》感兴趣，大概也会选择在Steam购买，而不会仅仅为了获得《暗黑破坏神4》的杰洛特皮肤，再在战网重新买一份《巫师3：狂猎》。
一名用户在社交媒体上表示：「我可不会为了一个大多数想玩的人估计早就已经买过的15年前老游戏，再花钱买第二份。不过还是谢谢你啊，暴雪。」另一名用户则针对座谈会现场图片中杰洛特的脸表示：「他看起来太糟糕了。不过我反倒挺高兴，因为我完全不想为了这个东西，在史上最差的启动器上预购游戏。我真的希望他们以后能把这款皮肤单独拿出来卖。」
杰洛特皮肤也遭到了一些《暗黑破坏神4》玩家的批评，因为暴雪昨天已经确认，这款游戏未来不会再推出任何资料片，这让部分玩家感到不满。《暗黑破坏神》游戏总监Brent Gibson告诉PC Gamer：「我们现在全部专注于《暗黑破坏神4》的赛季内容，以及朝着《暗黑破坏神5》推进。我们认为『憎恨之章』的故事已经讲完了。在『憎恨之王』中，围绕墨菲斯托的故事已经有了一个很好的结局，现在我们正在朝着讲述『恐惧之章』的方向前进。」
《暗黑破坏神4》于2023年6月发售。《暗黑破坏神5》计划于2029年的某个时候推出。谈到杰洛特皮肤时，Tost在暴雪嘉年华的Battle.net座谈会上表示：「从创作角度来说，这类合作对我们来说特别有趣，因为它会让我们这些创作者不得不去思考：怎样才能让两个世界发生碰撞，同时又能尊重这两部原作——在这个案例中，就是《暗黑破坏神》和《巫师》？所以面对这类合作时，我们首先会尝试寻找两边的交集。什么东西是合理的？说到《暗黑破坏神》的职业，在查看现有职业阵容之后，我们很快就觉得野蛮人是最适合加入杰洛特风格内容的地方。两者都是身体能力方面的高手。他们终其一生都在接受训练，让自己成为极其强壮、强大的近战战士。野蛮人能够同时携带多种武器。杰洛特虽然不会同时使用它们，但他确实使用两把剑：标志性的钢剑用来对付人类，银剑则用来对付怪物。大家也可以在这里看到——熟悉的人应该一眼就能认出来——这套护甲在很大程度上受到了杰洛特经典凯尔·莫罕护甲的启发，同时又加入了一些野蛮人的元素……比如你能看到大量毛皮。我想，从这里大家应该能看出，我们在制作这类联动时，会尽量让它对双方团队、两个世界以及双方粉丝来说都合情合理。我希望大家能看出来，我们创造出的东西放进庇护之地后也显得非常自然。」
CD Projekt表示，明年还会有更多《巫师》主题内容加入《暗黑破坏神4》，更多细节将在之后公布。CD Projekt介绍：「这款将杰洛特风格带入庇护之地地狱景象中的皮肤，是首个加入《暗黑破坏神4》的《巫师》主题内容，此外还有更多内容正在制作，并将于2027年加入暴雪的这款动作RPG。」
随着CD Projekt与暴雪之间的合作进一步扩大，CD Projekt宣布《赛博朋克2077》、资料片《往日之影》以及终极版将在今年晚些时候登陆战网。与此同时，暴雪旗下《守望先锋》将在2027年推出以《赛博朋克：边缘行者》和《边缘行者2》为主题的内容。续作动画剧集《赛博朋克：边缘行者2》将于10月20日在Netflix上线。

title: 《暗黑破坏神4》「地狱遗赠」赛季实机演示
text:
探寻庇护之地至暗传奇的遗赠
三位曾寄宿过魔神的黑暗流浪者自混沌界归来，将昔日的梦魔带回世间。跟随迪卡德·凯恩灵魂的指引，踏入他们支离破碎的记忆，直面塑造他们宿命的恐惧，探寻庇护之地至暗传奇的遗赠。《暗黑破坏神4》「地狱遗赠」赛季将于9月16日上线。

title: 《战争机器：事变日》宣传视频
text:
将于10月6日发售
《战争机器：事变日》故事发生在初代《战争机器》的十四年前，你将与马可斯、多姆一同，踏上这场扣人心弦的起源故事战役。游戏将于10月6日登陆XBOX Series及PC平台。

title: 《暗黑破坏神4》「地狱遗赠」赛季预告
text:
跟随迪卡德·凯恩灵魂的指引
三位曾寄宿过魔神的黑暗流浪者自混沌界归来，将昔日的梦魔带回世间。跟随迪卡德·凯恩灵魂的指引，踏入他们支离破碎的记忆，直面塑造他们宿命的恐惧，探寻庇护之地至暗传奇的遗赠。《暗黑破坏神4》「地狱遗赠」赛季将于9月16日上线。

title: 《End of Abyss》开发幕后
text:
直面游荡于此的恐怖怪物
在一处神秘地下基地的深处，一场调查不明来源异动的任务逐渐演变为穿越破败废弃世界的惊魂之旅。扮演年轻的战斗技术员Cel，直面游荡于此的恐怖怪物，同时揭开设施荒废区域的真相。《End of Abyss》将于10月1日登陆PS5、XBOX Series及PC（Epic游戏商城）平台。

title: 《黎明行者之血》媒体赞誉宣传视频
text:
塑造成属于你的故事
《黎明行者之血（The Blood of Dawnwalker）》是一款开放世界黑暗奇幻动作RPG。故事背景在14世纪的欧洲，你将扮演科恩，一名白昼时为人类，黑夜时为吸血鬼的年轻人。在为了拯救家人的奋斗之中，所做出的各种抉择与揭露的秘密，将塑造成属于你的故事。《黎明行者之血》现正在PS5、XBOX Series和PC平台发售。

title: 《猎杀：对决 1896》「血魔」预告
text:
嗜血者已于血月之时留下印记
他曾是不惜一切寻找解药的普通人。而今，他变成了那个他一心想要摆脱的怪物。林奇的执念无边无际，任何阻碍都无法停下她追寻的脚步。嗅觉。味觉。触觉。所有本能，万千思绪，无尽渴望。全部被一样东西吞噬：鲜血。这份嗜血的渴望，永远填不满……嗜血者已于血月之时留下印记，成功令猎物流血。这份奖赏现已降临，但在部分人眼中，它更像是一场诅咒。

title: 《间谍密令外传》实机预告
text:
单枪匹马潜入敌方基地
《间谍密令外传（Spy Drop Gaiden）》背景设定在日本近海的一座岛屿。玩家需要潜入密不透风的敌方基地，执行一系列机密任务，以消除全球威胁。单枪匹马潜入敌方基地，在敌众我寡的绝境中执行各类任务：从解救囚犯到收集情报，再到操控无人机深入敌占区展开行动。游戏将于10月12日登陆PC平台。

title: 《编年史：中世纪》「战斗」概览预告
text:
置身于广袤中世纪沙盒世界的中心
在《编年史：中世纪（Chronicles: Medieval）》中，你将置身于广袤中世纪沙盒世界的中心。你参与的战斗、组建的军队以及做出的决策，都将塑造你的征程。战斗，是这一切的核心。数百名士兵在你周围厮杀——军旗林立，刀剑交鸣。你一边实时指挥部队，一边与士兵并肩作战，从籍籍无名的小卒，成长为留名青史的人物。书写你的传奇，铸就你的威名！游戏将于2027年登陆PC平台。

title: 《怪物猎人 荒野：凌越》「斩斧」武器介绍视频
text:
迎战强大的怪物
启动「增幅护腕」后，猎人的动作性能会在一定时间内得到强化，并可使用全新招式与派生。通过启动「增幅护腕」并同时施展强力攻击的新动作「增幅发动动作」，以及活用能在一定时间内强化各种动作的「增幅状态」，迎战强大的怪物。超大型扩充内容《怪物猎人 荒野：凌越》目前正在开发中，将于2027年推出，《凌越》将会延续《怪物猎人 荒野》主线剧情，追加全新故事、新的原野和怪物、猎人动作，以及新增「大师等级」任务等级等各种内容。

title: 《暗黑破坏神5》已进入全面开发阶段，这里有6个新细节
text:
《暗黑破坏神5》已经正式进入全面制作阶段，并将于2029年推出。游戏总监Joe Shely透露，续作将拥有更多职业、程序化生成世界，并把时间线推进到100年之后。
尽管《暗黑破坏神》系列还有大量新内容即将推出，包括全新的Netflix剧集、《暗黑破坏神4》第15赛季、Switch 2版本等，但在2026年暴雪嘉年华上，该系列最重磅的消息还是《暗黑破坏神5》正式公布，并确认将于2029年推出。
IGN独家采访了这款新作背后的开发团队，包括游戏总监Joe Shely、叙事总监Jennifer Helper和制作总监Tiffany Wat。几位开发者透露了大量有关《暗黑破坏神5》的新细节，其中包括游戏目前已经度过早期开发阶段。
IGN：我想应该没人错过《暗黑破坏神5》的公布，不过你们能不能先从整体层面介绍一下，这款游戏会是什么样的？
Joe Shely：《暗黑破坏神5》的世界里，庇护之地已经沦陷，迪亚波罗取得了胜利。这意味着整个世界正处于末日之中。多年以来，玩家在历代《暗黑破坏神》游戏里一直试图阻止的那个结局，最终还是发生了。其他英雄曾经挺身而出，试图阻止迪亚波罗，但他们失败了。迪亚波罗如今坐在威斯特玛的王座上，并征服了整个西方大陆。
《暗黑破坏神5》的故事背景设定在《暗黑破坏神4》100年后的原因
IGN：《暗黑破坏神4》显然还有相当长的生命周期。你们希望在《暗黑破坏神5》中实现哪些事情，是你们认为整体上无法在《暗黑破坏神4》里实现的？
Joe Shely：《暗黑破坏神4》仍然会得到充分支持，团队会继续全力支持这款游戏。就在今天早些时候，我们才刚刚公布了即将加入《暗黑破坏神4》的亚马逊、第15赛季「地狱遗赠」，《暗黑破坏神4》也将登陆Switch 2，而且之后仍会继续获得支持。玩家有很多理由继续玩下去。当然，我们也已经开发《暗黑破坏神5》有一段时间了。现在游戏已经进入全面制作阶段，对我们来说，终于能够把它分享给玩家，真的是一个非常令人兴奋的时刻。
Jennifer Helper：我们要让迪亚波罗回归，而在一款《暗黑破坏神》游戏里，迪亚波罗绝不应该只是「另外还有一个东西」。我们需要一整个围绕迪亚波罗展开的完整战役和完整故事。在《暗黑破坏神5》中，我们把时间线向后推进了100年，以此来讲述这个故事。这样一来，在我们开发《暗黑破坏神5》的同时，《暗黑破坏神4》依然拥有足够大的空间去继续发展自己的故事和内容。
《暗黑破坏神5》将拥有「比你以往见过的还要多的职业」
Tiffany Wat：《暗黑破坏神5》给了我们一个机会，让我们真正能够深入运用一些非常出色的创新，不只是技术层面，也包括玩法和系统层面。
我们会带来比历代任何一款《暗黑破坏神》都更多的职业。我们也谈到了回归程序化生成世界，这是过去《暗黑破坏神》游戏中非常受欢迎的一项设计，而在《暗黑破坏神4》里，我们也通过地下城系统沿用了其中的一部分。到了《暗黑破坏神5》，我们确实觉得，这是一种非常有趣、同时也是《暗黑破坏神》游玩体验中不可或缺的方式，所以我们希望让它同时回归到大地图和地下城系统中。
Joe经常会和团队讨论「持续发现」的重要性，也就是说，你永远不知道拐角后面会出现什么。这会为庇护之地增加一种危险感，同时也与Jennifer和她的团队想讲述的故事非常契合。能够将所有这些元素融合在一起，并真正实现乔和他的团队的游戏目标，对我们来说，开发续作就顺理成章了。而实际上，我们已经做这件事有一段时间了。
《暗黑破坏神5》的开放世界程度会降低，因为迪亚波罗已经摧毁了一切
IGN：听起来你们更想回归那种传统的大地图结构，让玩家在不同区域之间移动。所以它不会再像《暗黑破坏神4》那样拥有开放世界的感觉，对吗？
Tiffany Wat：已经没有城镇了，因为迪亚波罗和他的恐惧指挥官已经彻底摧毁了庇护之地。所以，你所集结起来的那支商队，以及你一路遇到的那些成员——那些与你一同前进、只想努力活下来的庇护之地幸存者——会跟着你一起尝试生存下去，同时弄清楚迪亚波罗究竟在做什么。
你会从一个区域移动到另一个区域，而这也让我们有机会真正展现，当庇护之地落入恐惧之王统治后会变成什么样，以及不同的恐惧指挥官是如何扭曲这个世界的。Joe和我已经在《暗黑破坏神》的怪物设计上合作超过十年了，而现在怪物团队真的做出了很多东西。能够看到那些扭曲、恶心、恐怖的恶魔，在你进入不同世界时于不同时间出现，真的非常、非常酷。
IGN：等《暗黑破坏神5》发售时，看起来《暗黑破坏神4》和其他游戏仍然会继续得到支持。当你们实际上有五款《暗黑破坏神》游戏同时运营，让玩家一季又一季不断回来游玩时，你们是否预见到一些挑战？不仅是玩家留存方面，也包括整体内容制作方面。
Tiffany Wat：我们为每一款游戏都配备了专门的团队，因为这些游戏对我们来说很重要，对我们的社区也非常重要。我觉得这实际上给了我们一个非常好的机会，让不同团队能够彼此合作、相互交流。虽然我们可能是彼此独立的团队，但依然保持着非常紧密的合作，因为归根结底，我们都是在为《暗黑破坏神》社区制作游戏。我认为，现在是成为《暗黑破坏神》粉丝最好的时候。
《暗黑破坏神2》如何启发了《暗黑破坏神5》
IGN：ARPG市场正在不断扩大。当目标玩家群体被多个作品分流时，《暗黑破坏神》要如何继续进化？你们会不会观察这些游戏推出了哪些新东西，再考虑把类似元素加入自己的游戏？
Joe Shely：当然会。从根本上来说，ARPG在所有东西之下，本质上都是系统驱动的游戏。凡是和《暗黑破坏神》有关，或者可能让我们了解玩家正在享受什么的游戏，我们都会去玩。不过具体来说，我们的做法还是专注于那些真正属于《暗黑破坏神》核心、而且也是《暗黑破坏神》非常擅长的东西。例如不断进化我们的战斗模式，或者制作一款容易上手、同时拥有出色战役的游戏。我们希望这会成为我们有史以来最好的战役。
《暗黑破坏神2》里一些更有深度、更具系统感的东西，一直很受核心ARPG玩家欢迎，这也影响了《暗黑破坏神5》。例如装备的属性需求将会回归，还有装备等级设计，这一点很大程度上受到《暗黑破坏神2》的启发。甚至包括腰带栏位回归，以及物品会在背包中占据多个格子这样的设计。
腰带栏位回归
IGN：既然提到了，你能具体谈谈腰带栏位回归，以及《暗黑破坏神5》的装备系统与《暗黑破坏神4》相比，会采用怎样的设计思路吗？
Joe Shely：简单来说，腰带栏通常就是比裤子栏更有意思。腰带栏体现了我们对玩家可装备物品组合的考量。我们始终希望在这方面取得平衡，让玩家无论是在武器还是护甲方面，都有数量合适、种类不同的装备值得追求。因此，在视觉风格演变方面，腰带栏的优势之一在于能够让胸甲和裤子之间的装备套装更加协调统一。
重返西境
IGN：我们已经看到，迪亚波罗现在也要在《暗黑破坏神4》中回归，从第15赛季开始。距离《暗黑破坏神5》发售，中间还会有不知道多少个赛季。对于迪亚波罗在《暗黑破坏神4》里的呈现方式，以及之后他在《暗黑破坏神5》中的登场，你们有没有任何担忧？
Jennifer Helper：我们不仅把时间线推进了100年，同时也重新回到了西方大陆。《暗黑破坏神4》的内容全部发生在东方，而我们则回到了威斯特玛，这是大家通过前三部游戏都非常熟悉的地方。而且威斯特玛如今已经扩张到了整个西方大陆。因此，我们可以讲述西方大陆未来100年间发生的许多历史，而这个地方我们已经很久没有真正展现过了，所以对我们来说，这是一片完全开放的创作空间。
IGN：最后一个问题。我们什么时候能了解到更多《暗黑破坏神5》的消息？
Shely：当我们决定宣布正在开发《暗黑破坏神5》时，我们希望确保分享一些有意义的更新，比如职业方面的内容，猎魔人和武僧的回归，以及瘟疫骑士等新职业 ，还有我们之前讨论过的物品系统。我们希望继续这些讨论。尤其重要的是，我们现在谈论这款游戏，并将讨论延续到 2027 年（届时我们将分享更多内容），是为了能够与玩家交流，与所有热爱《暗黑破坏神》的人们交流，与他们一起打造游戏，倾听他们的心声。

title: 《新蝙蝠侠2》片场照暗示猫头鹰法庭将出现
text:
相关文章: 罗伯特·帕丁森：《新蝙蝠侠2》会走完全不同方向
来自《新蝙蝠侠2》伦敦片场的新视频和照片，进一步加剧了有关哥谭富豪精英秘密组织「猫头鹰法庭」将在影片中登场的传闻。
来自《新蝙蝠侠2》伦敦片场的新视频和照片显示，罗伯特·帕丁森饰演的布鲁斯·韦恩在警方护送下穿过一群愤怒的抗议者。这些画面进一步加剧了有关哥谭富豪精英秘密组织「猫头鹰法庭」将参与剧情的传闻，不过这些照片似乎也暗示，另一名蝙蝠侠系列中的反派可能同样会出现在影片中。 还有更多相关内容 《新蝙蝠侠2》新路透：蝙蝠车与哥谭警方街头冲突
社交媒体上的视频显示，导演马特·里夫斯正在拍摄这样一场戏：布鲁斯从哥谭律师协会的台阶上走下，在哥谭市警察局的保护下穿过大批抗议者，前往一辆等候中的宾利汽车，并在那里与由替身饰演的阿尔弗雷德·潘尼沃斯会面。阿尔弗雷德的演员安迪·瑟金斯目前正在新西兰执导并主演《指环王：追捕咕噜》。饰演吉姆·戈登的杰弗里·怀特也被拍到现身片场。
抗议者挥舞的标语牌揭示了他们愤怒的来源，同时也提供了有关猫头鹰法庭的第一个暗示，其中写着：「寡头法庭」「肮脏法庭」「富人越来越富」「总有一天穷人将一无所有」「反抗」「吃掉富人」「你们的贪婪正在害死我们」以及「寡头必须滚蛋！」现场还有一些带有蝙蝠侠元素的标语牌，比如一块写着「救救我们」，另一块则画着蝙蝠侠面具，并在下方写着「下一个就是你」。
这些画面中的讽刺之处显然在于，抗议者把这座城市最富有的人布鲁斯·韦恩视为敌人，却又把他的另一个身份蝙蝠侠当成反抗腐败体制的象征。最令人好奇的是，一些抗议者戴着完全遮住面部的白色面具。其中有一名蒙面抗议者的夹克上画着白色无政府主义符号，这种造型让人联想到游戏《蝙蝠侠：阿卡姆起源》中的反派「安纳奇」。这些蒙面抗议者会不会就是他的手下？
在DC漫画中，安纳奇是蝙蝠侠最具政治色彩的对手之一，他为了追求社会正义，会对政府和企业机构使用暴力。他本名朗尼·梅钦，也是蝙蝠侠最年轻的对手之一，有时甚至会被塑造成反英雄，而并非彻底的反派。
虽然安纳奇此前已经在真人剧集《绿箭侠》和动画《当心蝙蝠侠》中登场，但他从未出现在蝙蝠侠真人电影中。值得注意的是，马特·里夫斯此前曾表示，《新蝙蝠侠2》中的反派「以前从未真正出现在电影里」。当然，也有可能那张片场照里只是一个胸口带有无政府主义符号的普通群演，并不意味着安纳奇或他的运动会出现在这部电影里。我们这里只是在猜测。
话虽如此，如果一部电影同时加入猫头鹰法庭和安纳奇，其实非常符合马特·里夫斯版《蝙蝠侠》的风格，毕竟哥谭无处不在的腐败一直都是这个系列最核心的主题之一。

title: 本周 Steam 值得关注的游戏 09.14 - 09.20（一）
text:
本周将迎来 Steam 的“团队角色扮演游戏节”，新发售的游戏数量又多了不少，一起来看看吧！
注： 本系列文章的信息主要整合自 Steam 与 SteamDB 的即将发售列表，由于 Steam 支持手动输入日期及发售、同步不及时等原因，本列表可能会遗漏收录一些作品的发售信息。如果本周有您的作品或您喜欢的作品未被列出，欢迎直接评论补充链接～～
公会创世纪（Creator Chronicles）
关键字： AI 生成内容、管理、城市营造、角色扮演
发行日期： 2026/09/14（ 中文支持 ）
冒险为何而启，公会为何而兴？在战火席卷的大陆上，你将执掌公会，召集冒险小队开荒副本、完成首杀，体验经典 RPG 冒险！从地下城探索到史诗 Boss 挑战，获取装备、强化阵容。与此同时经营公会领地、建设城镇、调配资源，持续壮大势力，在这片传奇大陆再次写属于你的公会荣光！
How to Grow Your Sausage
关键字： 增量、打字、桌面伴侣
发行日期： 2026/09/14（暂无中文）
每次[按键]都会让你的香肠变大。把它放在屏幕角落，一边使用电脑，一边看着它长大。给它喂不同的肉，升级你的屠夫，见证奇迹的发生。你是否曾梦想过让香肠长大？现在终于可以实现了！
焕然一新的收纳生活（Neat!）
关键字： 整理、装饰、模拟
发行日期： 2026/09/14（ 中文支持 ）
不知不觉，生活和房间都变得一团乱？别担心，马上就会焕然一新！在《焕然一新的收纳生活》中，成为一名收纳师。整理房间、收纳物品，让杂乱的空间重现秩序。在轻松沉浸的整理过程中，倾听隐藏在杂乱背后的温情故事；在和解与自我成长中，释放长久累积的压力。体验治愈解压的收纳之旅，让心情与生活一同焕然一新。
锡吉尔法师（Sigilfarer: A Dice-Rolling Roguelite）
关键字： 骰子、牌组构建式类 Rogue、回合制战斗
发行日期： 2026/09/14（ 中文支持 ）
《锡吉尔法师》是一款类肉鸽类冒险游戏，每一个决定都取决于骰子的投掷。骰子构建游戏机制，广阔世界任你航行。策划你的路线，管理资源，并将你的运气推向极限！
米粒新世界（Pibcremental）
关键字： 模拟、挂机游戏、增量
发行日期： 2026/09/14（ 中文支持 ）
人类已经消失，只剩忙忙碌碌的米粒！在增量放置点击的过程中壮大族群，采集资源、培育树干、制造设施、扩散分工，并应对各类随机事件，让文明在郁郁葱葱的树冠之间繁衍生息，把桌面变成小家伙们的游乐场。
云上叠叠乐（Cloudscrapers）
关键字： 城市营造、休闲、解谜
发行日期： 2026/09/14（ 中文支持 ）
《云上叠叠乐》是一款具有放松氛围的极简策略游戏。建造你的高塔，管理资源，解锁新工具，探索隐藏在天空中的秘密。
The Headlands
关键字： 农场模拟、管理
发行日期： 2026/09/14（暂无中文）EA
一款以 00 年代为背景的充满冥想色彩的农场经营策略游戏：你的家乡，以及童年记忆中的那些农机。复兴一座破败的农场，在充满生机的市场上进行交易，运营生产链，承接邻居的订单，并逐步扩充你的车队——从小拖拉机到联合收割机。

幻鸟之森（Fantasy Bird Woods）

title: I've got a soft spot for cozy games with flying in them and these are my 4 favorites
text:
I lobbied to make Promise Mascot Agency the best cozy game in our 2025 Game of the Year awards, which means I'm only ( checks calendar ) a little late in getting it added to my list of best cozy games this week. I adore its silly story and open world exploration and got to thinking about how much fun it is to full throttle my kei truck right off the side of a cliff and press a button to sprout wings so I can soar peacefully around Kaso-Machi island.
It isn't even the only game with flying on the list now. It is in fact the third on that list of ten. I think I have a real soft spot for flying in cozy games.
There are as many definitions of "cozy game" as there are cozy gamers, but freedom is a really common element. There's freedom to build in life sims or freedom from time constraints in puzzle games. What is flying but complete and total freedom of exploration?
In the years since Breath of the Wild we've been spoiled for open world games with gliders, but a game with proper flying is even better. In Promise Mascot Agency I can hit my kei truck's boost thruster, nudge its nose up to gain altitude, and bank into a turn for a second pass over the rural sprawl below. It's the most open an open world can be and the freest I ever feel exploring one.
What are your favorite cozy games with flying in them? Bonus points if they really are flying, not gliding. Here are mine:
Promise Mascot Agency
Once you upgrade your kei truck with wings you are unstoppable. This thing is meant to be bashed and crashed into every obstacle you find, which is extra true once you can launch it off a switchback mountain road into an elegant nose dive directly onto a collectible you were looking for. Pure joy.
Journey
A classic from before the "cozy game" era, this one is all about increasing your flight distance as you progress through its short, emotional story. The ending of this one is the most pure distillation of the joy of flight.
Sky: Children of the Light
Also by the studio who made Journey, it has similar flight controls and distance upgrades, but it's a miniature MMO with tons of puzzles and exploration that I love going back to every few months.
A Short Hike
Technically, this one is gliding because I don't think you can gain altitude, but exploring the gorgeous lofi island in search of secret areas is exactly what makes flight so fun.

title: After more than 400 hours of Valheim in early access, I love the journey from naked adventurer to godly Viking now more than ever
text:
Play This Right Now
Welcome to Play This Right Now, the site version of our weekly newsletter in which we celebrate a new game, update, or DLC that we think is well worth checking out. You can subscribe to the newsletter at the link if you want to get our thoughts about a new videogame happening direct to your inbox every Thursday.
I'm back on my bullshit, and by bullshit I mean sinking another delightful 100 hours into Valheim —the Viking-themed survival crafting game that sits among my top five most-played games on Steam. With the launch of 1.0 and its new biome, the Deep North, now is the best time to round up your friends and return to ye olde old sea fortresses and swampy castles. A lot has changed in Odin's purgatory.
Or even better, forget your old worlds and start anew. The Deep North's endgame is its biggest draw, sure, but from start to finish, Valheim is a much better experience with boss reworks, small UI tweaks, and a few new cutscenes for a lovely pinch of world-building. You don't get a good look at the big picture by booting up old saves, and after diving into Valheim 1.0 with nothing but a wooden club and tattered leather loincloth, I can confidently say I don't regret it one bit.
Perhaps some of that is thanks to skipping last year's Call to Arms update—the patch where Iron Gate dramatically reworked the buffs received from slaying Valheim's giant gods—but now I'm glad I waited. As my total Valheim playtime rapidly approaches the 500-hour mark, I can't help but be impressed by how good a handful of small changes and new items make progression to the endgame feel.
Some of those changes stood out as soon as I entered the cozy Meadows of Valheim's starting zone, and I guarantee any survival-crafting, base-building menace like myself will be just as thrilled as I was to see Iron Gate's reworked building UI. Instead of endlessly scrolling through a sea of furniture, walls, and decor, I can finally search for and favorite individual pieces as a shortcut or create entire categories dedicated to my go-to tools. It's the first time in years I've enjoyed Valheim without a slew of QoL building mods.
(Image credit: Iron Gate Studios) I've already made biome-specific building collections for every zone too, and even have pared-down versions for quick access in emergencies. We're all guilty of picking fights with Fulings that we can't handle, but I like to pull the ol' Fortnite on 'em. That's code for building a box around myself and crying for help, by the way. Is that not how Fortnite works?
First-time Vikings or lapsed players like myself will also appreciate Valheim's smooth transition from the early-game Meadows to the fiery end-times hellscape of the Ashlands. With all of its pieces in alignment, you don't need your nose in a wiki or a posse of seasoned friends to figure out the next steps of the adventure.
There's a clearer big-picture path to Valheim we just didn't have before, and I'm finally comfortable recommending it as a version-complete build without all of the early access caveats.
(Image credit: Iron Gate Studios) The boss reworks from last year pair especially well with the breadcrumb directions added in 1.0's cutscenes, too. I won't spoil the whole thing for you, but historically, Valheim didn't do the best job of teaching its Vikings how to play. And I mean, it still doesn't deliver its secrets on a silver platter, but that's more fun when you've got a vague hint about where to go next and a series of boss buffs that all feel viable. Back in my day, we had seven boss buffs, and only one (or maybe two) of them felt viable.
Iron Gate also heard us loud and clear on the stingy storage space and how miserable navigating the foggy marble cliffs of the Mistlands felt. The Deep North update comes with upgradeable pocket space and a nifty grappling hook for safely traversing one of Valheim's most hostile zones—or so I'm told. You may be surprised to learn I've mostly used these upgrades for holding more decorations and slingshotting my Viking between taller building projects. What goes on in the Mistlands is none of my business.
This is all before you get to the Deep North, mind you. There are still plenty of secrets hidden in Valheim's last chapter, but it would be a shame to remember the journey to that point only by its early access builds. So whether you're playing for the first time or a seasoned Viking, I vote you all start the same way: naked in the Meadows, wielding a stick.
You can check out Valheim 1.0—out now on Steam .

title: My favourite soundtrack of 2026 so far is tucked in one of this year's biggest sleeper hits
text:
Critical Hit
(Image credit: Future) Welcome to Critical Hit , where I (or someone else on the PC Gamer team) celebrate and lament all things videogame music, audio design, and the ways our favourite games make our ears tingle.
I have not been able to stop thinking about Big Walk since I finished the game alongside six of my friends last month. What I had anticipated to be a relatively okay, quick-dirty-fun co-op game unfurled itself into one of the most thoughtful videogames I've ever played, and easily my favourite of 2026 so far. I cannot even begin to explain what a fantastic job developer House House has done at creating an incredibly special, unreplicatable experience that has had me and my pals continuing to talk about it in the weeks since we rolled credits.
While so much of its exceptionality lies in its puzzles (and all of the little moments in between), one of the biggest things I fell in love with was its music. It's a surprisingly sporadic facet of the game—Big Walk doesn't have a soundtrack that accompanies you everywhere, and you can go some real chunky stretches of time without hearing any music at all.
(Image credit: Panic) But in the little pockets of the world where it reveals itself, having it cut through the silence makes the moments you spend with it feel even more special. Spread across almost 30 tracks, Australian duo aksfx play around with these delightfully ethereal, pulsing beats and jumping vocals that sound like they should be mildly unsettling on paper, but the execution leads to this delightful feeling of exploration and airiness.
Tons of Big Walk's music is scattered across radio stations that you have to go and seek out, or simply stumble across as you're exploring and shooting the shit with your pals. These are some of my favourite locations in the game—the radio stations are fully immersive, spatial audio experiences thanks to each one being surrounded with speakers that let you really hear each and every component.
Not only are they moments of respite to bask in for a bit, but they're the perfect backdrop to punctuate cute moments with your pals. Coming across a radio station right as the sun is rising and taking a second to watch it happen as the notes delicately echo around you feels like something straight out of a slice-of-life anime's penultimate episode, the one that makes you bawl your eyes out.
And you can even take these pieces of music around with you if the silence isn't quite your thing. Big Walk lets you strap the radios to someone's backpack, turning them into a walking boombox/audial beacon. It's a lovely little choice on House House's part—I took great pleasure in carrying one such radio around with me for hours, and when we finally deposited it I actually felt a little bit sad.
For me, though, aksfx's magnum opus comes from Big Walk's theme itself. It's the first thing you hear when you boot up the game—jumping vocals evoke this odd sense of nostalgia before you've even ventured into the lobby for the first time. And when you've rolled credits 10 or so hours in? It hits even harder, and has me tearing up just a little bit every time I listen to it.
The cosiness it adds to the overall experience, and the fact that just a few vocal chops can get the waterworks going? Well, that's what videogame music is all about, isn't it? Making us feel things, both in the moment and even detached from its original context thanks to the memories it brings along with it.
There are so many reasons to love Big Walk, and its music is certainly up there as one of my biggest. Much like the game's concept, puzzles, and little three-blobbed players, the game's soundtrack may be simple at first glance, but its execution brings so much depth that I hadn't anticipated.

title: YouTuber runs onto the stage at Roblox Developers Conference shouting 'We deserve better,' gets tackled and ejected from show
text:
Over the last few days, Roblox's 2026 Developers Conference was held in San Jose, California, and one of Roblox CEO David Baszucki's on-stage introduction's hit something of a hitch. Roblox YouTuber Mathieo took to the stage shouting, "We deserve better, don't we deserve better," while revealing a shirt that read "Kids deserve better," until he was quickly tackled and escorted out.
yoooo what #robloxㅤ pic.twitter.com/ZH3VJNGti0 September 11, 2026
Baszucki played the incident off in the moment, saying "We all get a little excited when RDC comes along, as we just saw." But it was shared online by X user bearpuppyrbx, prompting a quote-repost from Mathieo himself—"just got kicked out #rdc26 💔," he wrote . He explained his stunt the same day in a short YouTube video uploaded to his channel.
"I know there's a lot of people that really love RDC, and I'm glad people are enjoying themselves," he said in the video. "My issue isn't with the people. I just do believe that Roblox [Corporation] isn't as dumb as they say they are … everybody's saying they don't want AI. Everybody's saying they don't want these faces messed up. Everybody wants better child safety.
"Every single slow year of progress is just another year where children are actually affected."
Roblox's dubious child safety measures have been criticized for a number of years. It has recently introduced child accounts in an attempt to address the issue, the US Senate is actively investigating the platform , and legislation like the EU's Digital Services Act aim to force Roblox Corporation's hand in protecting minors.
The game has been called a " pedophile hellscape " by one investment firm, and Baszucki has put his foot in his mouth on this several times in the past—take, for instance, that time he suggested Roblox become a dating hub , or that disastrous interview he had with the New York Times where he suggested "the problem of predators on Roblox" was "not necessarily just as a problem, but an opportunity as well."
"We've seen that telling them just doesn't work," Mathieo said in the video. "It's been many years now where this has been a really prevalent issue. And while they're 'finding a fix,' there's probably a lot of kids that have been harmed on Roblox recently."
I have reached out to the Roblox Corporation for comment on the incident, and will update this story if I hear back.

title: Fallout dev Tim Cain says the games industry's volatility is 'always gonna be around': 'What's happening now isn't novel, it isn't new'
text:
I don't know if you've noticed, but the games industry kind of sucks . Despite (and because of) the absurd amount of money games rake in, there's an ungodly degree of consolidation , the RAMpocalypse , and constant, huge waves of layoffs . Tim Cain, who co-created the original Fallout, uploaded a video to YouTube last Wednesday explaining why he thinks the current state of affairs is so terrible, if not terribly surprising.
"Why are things looking particularly bad right now? Well, the simple answer is 'cause they are bad right now," he said in the video. "Correction for [reckless investment during] COVID, hardware costs have shot up—a lot due to AI data centers—but investors are redirecting their money outside of the games industry, in some cases outside of the US … things had to contract. And that means people are gonna get laid off.
"These things will pass. They really will. I know if you're caught up in it, you're thinking, 'this is terrible.' They'll pass. That's the good news. The bad news is, new ones are gonna happen."
Cain was careful in his video to clarify that he understands things are uniquely bad now, but also said that things have been bad and will be bad again. "If you're somebody who got into the games industry in that time period, in the last five or 10 years, and you thought it was going to be a stable job that would see through 30 or 40 years, you assumed incorrectly. You're wrong."
He warned taking a decadeslong career like his own as evidence that gamdev work is reliable for up-and-comers was "survivorship bias." He recalled the stateside video game crash of 1983 as an example of what he introduced as his main point: "What's happening now isn't novel, it isn't new to the industry, and it's always gonna be around." As for why that is, he posited that games sit at the intersection between art and cutting-edge tech, both of which change rapidly as a rule.
For workers trying to weather industry conditions anyway, he suggested either honing an eclectic and broad set of skills or hyper-specializing and becoming a go-to guy in a particular niche. Notably, there is also a larger fight for labor rights in the industry trying to change some of these conditions for good: Blizzard Entertainment workers, for instance, just won what the Communications Workers of America called " a breakthrough first contract " for all the studio's game development teams and shared services. The Independent Workers of Great Britain, meanwhile, is currently rallying in support of Rockstar Games workers as the company grapples with union-busting allegations .

title: Discussing 20 years of Company of Heroes with the team carrying its torch into the future
text:
I still remember the PC Gamer cover from October 2006 featuring Company of Heroes as the vanguard of the "RTS Revolution." This was back in the day that I would walk down to the local grocery store to grab each new physical issue off of the news stand. I had just turned 17. I was already failing trigonometry. And in my free time, I was building a lightsaber hilt out of parts from the hardware store for Halloween… and trying to keep my airborne troops alive behind German lines on my first proper gaming PC.
At Relic Entertainment in Vancouver that same fall, as one designer recalled, Wagner's 'Ride of the Valkyries' played over the PA system as part of a ritual when one of their games finally went gold. I didn't encounter anything quite that dramatic when I visited earlier this summer to talk with the team about the 20th anniversary of the franchise, but even through all the ups and downs, I did find myself surrounded by people very excited to be making a World War 2 RTS.
A lot of the earliest history of the franchise has been scattered to the wind, unfortunately. The genesis of the idea, I was told, was a story only recalled by a small number of people who have since moved on from Relic, if not the industry altogether. I did learn that the original prototype was created in the engine from Impossible Creatures, a very strange 2003 RTS about creating hybridized animals to fight for you. But Company of Heroes certainly wears its influences on its bloodstained sleeve in a way that remains apparent even today.
"We were highly influenced by Saving Private Ryan and Band of Brothers," principal programmer Ian Thomson recalled. "That was the era where big leaps in visual quality were arriving, with the Half-Life 2 presentations blowing our mind with characters and physics. We wanted to bring that to RTS in a World War 2 setting."
I was barely old enough to see an R-rated movie on my own, of course, and I hadn't, at the time, watched either Spielberg's epic or HBO's landmark series. I was very familiar with the visual language of them, though, having grown up on Battlefield 1942, Medal of Honor, and the original Call of Duty. But even in shifting the perspective on those brutal D-Day landings from first-person to a bird's eye, I remember very little was lost in terms of drama and terror in the opening moments of the campaign.
The Human Element
Relic describes this phenomenon that got its hooks into me as "Humanizing the Battlefield," which they consider a core component to the franchise. In Company of Heroes, the audio and the animations, even outside of cutscenes, made me feel like these little soldiers I was ordering around were real people with lives back home they hoped to return to. They would take cover. They had morale, and could get pinned down or flee if they came under heavy fire.
Your average marine in Starcraft is basically an action figure. But when I zoomed in really close to an infantry squad in Company of Heroes, I found myself imagining: that one is Joe from Tennessee, and I could picture his cat, and the signed baseball on his dresser, and the kinds of pies his mom made for Thanksgiving. It sounds a little twee and overwrought, maybe, but they sold the illusion.
Relic was in the middle of a generational run, too, having almost completely reinvented the RTS formula a few years earlier with the original Dawn of War. After years of Warcrafts and Starcrafts and Commands and Conquers, Ages of Empires, they threw out a lot of the basic design of resource harvesting and base building and made a new breed of strategy game that was all about cover, momentum, and territory control. Another piece of why Company of Heroes felt so much more real is that its incentives led to the kinds of maneuvers and firefights a real battlefield commander might employ.
As for how they pulled this off, it may have simply been the boldness not to cut any corners.
"One of the defining characteristics of the CoH team was that nobody knew how to say no," principal programmer Remy Saville recalled. "Every time someone had a cool idea, we'd find a way to squeeze it in. Cover systems, destructible environments, squad tactics, all of it. The result was a game absolutely packed with features because the team was constantly pushing for more."
Apparently they really knew they had something when, Saville reminisced, people stopped taking lunch breaks just to stay at their desks and play more Company of Heroes. This same maximalist attitude, however, might have contributed to getting the team in trouble down the line. But for now, things were only looking up. Company of Heroes shipped as the highest rated RTS in PC Gamer's history with a 96—still one of the highest scores we've ever given to this day. It would receive two successful expansions, with Opposing Fronts in 2007 and Tales of Valor in 2009.
Into the Cold
(Image credit: Relic Entertainment) Discussions of a sequel were already in motion not long after the first game shipped. And while the first had focused mainly on the British, French, and American experiences on the Western Front, it seemed natural to head East for the next chapter. It would be a long wait for 2013's Company of Heroes 2. Long enough that the kid from before who had been failing trigonometry had made her way out to San Francisco to be an intern at the very magazine she'd once walked to the store to snag every month.I still remember seeing the demo for CoH2 in the office for the first time, before it had even been revealed to the public. It is a very different game. And in keeping up with a bit of a pattern that started with Dawn of War 2, it became another Relic sequel that took some big, divisive swings, and I ended up enjoying even more than the original.
The Eastern Front as Relic depicted it was a warscape defined just as much by Mother Nature's contributions as our own manufactured lead and steel. Infantry left out in the cold too long could actually suffer frostbite. Frozen lakes and rivers could be blown up with grenades, sending tanks plunging into the icy depths. I absolutely loved it. It's still my favorite game in the series, and we might never get anything like it again. But it was not universally embraced, especially by the competitive multiplayer community.
This put Relic in a bit of an awkward spot that I've seen various studios have to navigate. When you release something as genuinely iconic and beloved as Company of Heroes, the follow-up can't just be more of the same. It has to bring something new to the conversation. And inevitably, not everyone will love those new things. Where once the spirit of throwing every cool idea into one game had produced a hit, now it had resulted in a wave of backlash.
Far from being panned, however, our own Rich McCormick wrote in his review, scoring an 80, "sometimes clumsy, a game that can't maintain all its systems, with too many disparate moving parts to feel consistently coherent. But the final result, despite the small losses along the way, is a winner."
Still, the narrative had started to crystalize in the ice that maybe Relic had lost a little bit of that magic from the 2000s. Company of Heroes 2 was good, but not as good as the original, so you'd hear around RTS enthusiasts. And with Dawn of War 3 turning out even more disappointing a few years later, that started to become something almost like common wisdom.I wasn't fully buying it, though. And the biggest reason was a little expansion pack released in 2014 called Ardennes Assault. Taking place on a dynamic map meant to simulate the Battle of the Bulge, it allowed you to move troops around from province to province between RTS skirmishes to cut off enemy retreats and reinforcements. I distinctly remember this as the peak of Company of Heroes as a franchise. Its voiced commanders with rich backstories, reactive campaign AI, and the way it really forced me to pick my battles wisely kept me coming back to it even years later.
Bella, Ciao
(Image credit: Sega) When it came time to start thinking about Company of Heroes 3, that spirit of wanting to go big hadn't left the team at all. Looking at the positive reception to Ardennes Assault, an idea started to form of an even larger dynamic campaign set during the lesser-known liberation of Italy. At the time, Relic was working with Sega, who was also in charge of the Total War series. And from my perspective, the influence of modern Total War campaigns seemed apparent.
The problem is that it just didn't work very well. I remember being asked what I thought of Company of Heroes 3 at launch by a colleague and saying the RTS battles were as good as they'd ever been in the series, but the Italian campaign… well, that was kind of rough. Our own Fraser Brown concluded, in what was otherwise a mostly positive review, "right now it's impossible to look at it as anything other than a failure."
"Yeah, we bit off more than we could chew," Relic CEO Justin Dowdeswell told me very frankly. "The idea was great. The spirit of it was good. The team was energized. It was just more than we could get done in time, and that's it."
The road only got rockier in the aftermath of what ended up being a rough launch for Company of Heroes 3. The studio faced two rounds of layoffs, representing a large percentage of their overall staff, in 2023 and 2024. Many of the people I remember talking to regularly when covering Company of Heroes 3 were no longer around when I visited to discuss the current state of things. After the announcement that Dawn of War 4 was being developed by German studio King Art Games—I was later told Relic passed on it as they simply didn't have the bandwidth to take it on alongside other ongoing projects, mostly related to Company of Heroes—I was wondering if there even would be a Relic anymore.But in the meantime, they have split from Sega and become independent again. And while a smaller team than they were at their height, what I saw in Vancouver this summer was a company of coders, artists, audio engineers, and programmers who seemed to be in high spirits. While the ordeals of the last few years would be enough to break the morale of even seasoned troops in the streets of Carentan, they all seemed to be excited about continuing to work on this franchise.And it's still chugging along, with the recent release of the wave-based Final Stand mode last month.
Battles to Come
(Image credit: Relic Entertainment) The picture isn't exactly clear yet for what the next chapter of Company of Heroes might be called."The last chapter was called 'Chaos,' I know that," Dowdeswell quipped.
But there is a team with a drive to write it. The franchise, at the moment, might seem like it's knee-deep in seawater, under heavy German machine gun fire, just trying to make it to that shingle, especially without a large publisher like Sega providing air support.
"We will survive and thrive based on the success of the decisions that we make along the way," Dowdeswell said of their newfound independence. "And I think there's been, I don't know if it's a cultural shift, but a mood shift at the studio once everyone really started to see that it is up to us. The things we do can make a difference for the better, and when things go well, it was us. And I think that it removes any sort of question around, well, whose fault was that? Or whose win was that? Well, it's ours, either way, and I think that's more empowering than difficult."As a Company of Heroes fan, I hope to see this scrappier, independent Relic push forward to victory in spite of the setbacks they've faced since they first got off the landing craft 20 years ago. It won't be easy. But the commanding officers at the front seem to have no delusions that it will be."The industry's in turmoil, and this wasn't a guaranteed outcome for the studio," Dowdeswell concluded. "So I'm really pleased that we're here, able to support the games, and able to celebrate this 20th anniversary."
So am I. I'll crack a cold one to remember my boy Johnny Vastano from Ardennes Assault and send my best wishes to all the former Relic devs who I couldn't share one with on this trip, as tumult continues to follow after just about anyone involved in making games. We've lost a lot already, and I'd hate to lose Company of Heroes. So it's good to see that they're keeping up the fight.

title: StarCraft is a narrative-driven shooter with 'a definitive ending' and 'not a seasonal game'
text:
Following the announcement of a new StarCraft game at BlizzCon's Opening Ceremony, GM and creative director Dan Hay (best known for Far Cry 3-6) spoke to Korean media about the open-world shooter.
Based on Inven Global's transcript , it sounds like StarCraft will be a shooter along the lines of the Far Crys, though with a customizable lead character, and not a live service multiplayer game.
"If I were to describe the overall structure we currently envision, it's a 'box product,'" said Hay. "It is a narrative-driven open world shooter where players create a character, name them, and follow that character's story. The story has a beginning, a middle, and an end.
"You can roam around and explore a rich open world, but our story has a definitive ending. Think of it as purchasing a standalone boxed game, playing it, and experiencing its story. We hope players enjoy it, love it, and return to us later. At the very least, what we are building right now is not a seasonal game."
That's not what I expected to hear after seeing the cinematic trailer, which depicts a confident young soldier progressing through training before being unceremoniously turned to mush by Zerg. It projected Helldivers more than "standalone boxed game," and I'm still not 100% convinced that some kind of co-op or shared world multiplayer feature isn't going to appear between now and 2030.
Later in the conversation, Hay reveals a little more about StarCraft's structure, distinguishing between "serious missions" with narrative consequences and open world exploration, saying that "if a certain mission feels too difficult, you can return to the open world and engage in other activities at your own pace."
"If you lack adequate gear, you can head out into the world, scavenge for what you need, deck out your armor, and try again," Hay said. "... I like wandering around slowly, exploring, discovering new things, and encountering unexpected turns."
Hay also said that StarCraft is set 70 years after the events of StarCraft 2, which freed them up narratively.
"Thanks to that, we can build new stories, adventures, and characters," he said. "Factions that looked a certain way in the past might have shifted their perspectives over 70 years, disagreed with each other, or fractured into splinters. These changes provide ample room to forge new narratives. It's crucial to tell a new story while preserving StarCraft's signature dark, gritty mood and space western atmosphere."
StarCraft isn't scheduled to release until 2030. Following the announcement, Blizzard published several related job listings .

title: World of Warcraft Forever hype dampened by $30 elves: New Skyborne race locked behind expansion-tier purchase
text:
As noted by MMORPG.com , World of Warcraft: Forever is coming with a peculiar economic proposition: Most of the new fork of the MMO is included in your normal WoW subscription (rad), but the new Skyborne Elf race (and its corresponding starter zone experience) is gated behind a separate, $30 purchase (sad).
While "$30 elf" might be a somewhat uncharitable characterization, there's not much else that really lights my fire in the $29.99 "Skyborne Hero Pack." In addition to the titular elves, it comes with a mount, cosmetics, housing decorations, and early name reservation.
Compared to the bleeding edge of Overwatch, League of Legends, and Diablo premium cosmetic pricing, this is just keeping pace. But with many of the best new games on Steam coming in at $20 or less, I'm feeling sticker shock.
$30, for my money, is the cost of an expansion pack under normal economic conditions, though WoW's most recent retailed for $50 MSRP. Speaking to my WoW consultant and on-the-ground BlizzCon contact, PCG contributor Tyler Colp, he wagered that any new classes coming down the line in Forever will likely be similarly monetized, and argued that this sort of monetization is less in the spirit of classic WoW than the rest of the Forever project.
Looking at it from the outside, getting so much of the rest of Forever with a normal WoW subscription strikes me as an excellent bargain, but it only throws the $30 elf into even sharper relief as a consequence. Personally, I'd be more amenable to a $15 elf as a matter of principle, but I've been out of the MMO/live service game for some time. Do you think this is a fair market value for an elf? Sound off in the comments.

title: Warcraft 3: Reforged adds always-online requirement, removes LAN mode
text:
Warcraft 3: Reforged got a hefty 3.0 patch alongside its new Forsaken Kingdom expansion , but not all of the changes are for the better. Amid bugfixes and new features, Reforged now requires an internet connection to play, even in singleplayer, and it also removed the game's local area network (LAN) functionality. Blizzard did not provide a reason for these changes in the patch notes.
Blizzard does mention that LAN support and offline play are still offered by the legacy Warcraft 3 client included with purchase of Reforged. The company has a Battle.net support page with instructions on how to install this legacy client.
But it's still a frustrating, confounding change: Reforged was an embattled remaster that had to claw back support from the fanbase. The Forsaken Kingdom expansion and 3.0 patch were the perfect opportunity to complete a redemption arc and lock in Reforged as the definitive version of the 2002 RTS. But as much as things have improved, it's taken a stumble in its victory lap.
Always-online requirements have been a sore spot in gaming since they first started cropping up in the 2010s, and depending on where you live, reliable high-speed internet isn't always a guarantee. Even in the big city, outages aren't unheard of, and always-online requirements for singleplayer games remain an odious imposition on players.
The LAN removal makes even less sense to me: LAN party and tournament play have always struck me as an essential part of Warcraft 3's legacy. Why concede this ground to the original game when the remaster's reputation has been so contested since its release? You can check out the full Warcraft 3: Reforged patch notes over on the Blizzard forums. More positive changes include a new graphics mode and a doubling of the unit selection cap from 12 to 24.

title: 10 big World of Warcraft Forever details from BlizzCon: No separate realms, optional transmog, and massively improved items
text:
World of Warcraft Forever might be stuck in the first year of the MMO for the foreseeable future, but it's going to draw from future iterations of it to freshen up the experience.
Blizzard held a panel at BlizzCon today where WoW Forever developers dug into the crucial design changes that will differentiate it from the WoW Classic we already have. This version of the MMO doesn't sound like it'll be as much of a grind as the OG with its revised classes, talent trees, and all-new mechanics for pulling strangers together in the open world.
Many of the changes seem to fill in the gaps of the original WoW experience so that there's several things to chase as you explore Azeroth. Developers broke down how the MMO will bring players together, how the new "Legacy" progression system works, and how new and old items will influence combat.
Here are the big takeaways from the WoW Forever panel:
You pick a ruleset (e.g. normal, PvP, hardcore)—not a realm—to play on, which means you'll run into a lot more players on your journey than the other versions of WoW
Changing the appearance of your gear to look like other gear (transmog) is now a global setting you can turn on or off for you and other players
Looting most gear will grant everyone the transmog appearance automatically
Everyone can set up a campfire where other players can craft or rest for exclusive buffs via their professions
Each profession has over 600 new recipes across all level ranges
New race/class combinations include: Gnome priests, Human hunters, Dwarf shamans, Orc mages, Troll warlocks, and Undead paladins—and more are coming in the future
As you progress, you'll earn Legacy points to unlock various perks that alter how certain mechanics work, like removing the materials you need to cast major buffs, and obtain cosmetics
Most items in the game have been reworked (or new ones have been added) so that they're useful to all classes and roles
All bosses have better loot overall
The unique racial abilities for every playable race have been improved, and new ones have been added as well
There are a lot more details, especially for how popular abilities will work, explained in the panel. Part of the goal, Blizzard said, was to "unsolve" the game and give players a reason to experiment again.
It won't be a long wait to see how it all comes together. WoW Forever will launch on November 4 and will be playable under the same subscription as regular WoW. A beta will go live on Thursday, September 17, which you can access by purchasing the game early.

title: Cyberpunk 2077 is coming to Battle.net for some reason, and Geralt will be in Diablo 4
text:
Wouldn't it be nice if more of Blizzard's classic games were available on Steam? People could easily play them on their Steam Decks! But no, that's not happening. Instead, we're getting Cyberpunk 2077 on Battle.net.
After announcing at GamesCom that The Witcher 3's upcoming remastered version would release on Battle.net as well as the expected platforms, Blizzard and CD Projekt have announced at BlizzCon that Cyberpunk 2077 and its expansion will release there later this year. They'll be joining other non-Blizzard games everyone forgets are available on Battle.net like Sea of Thieves, Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3+4, and The Outer Worlds 2.
Diablo 2 Resurrected, Diablo 4, and Overwatch remain the only Blizzard games available on Steam. The original Diablo is still on GOG , though the first two Warcraft games were pulled from that storefront when they were remastered a couple of years ago.
The collaboration between Blizzard and CD Projekt will also be bringing Geralt to Diablo 4 in the form of a skin for the barbarian class, which will be available to players who prepurchase The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past DLC on Battle.net, with more "Witcher-themed content" threatened for 2027. Next year will also see Edgerunners-themed cosmetics coming to Overwatch. The show's second season will premiere on Netflix on October 20.

title: Diablo 5 will fully support multiplayer, but Blizzard won't say how similar to Diablo 4 it'll be
text:
Diablo 5 may be set in a lonely world ravaged by a demon lord, but you'll still be able to team up with your friends like in previous Diablo games.
Senior game director Joe Shely confirmed that Diablo 5 will fully support multiplayer in a group interview with PC Gamer: "Like Diablo 4, it is a game that you can play solo or multiplayer, however you please, and you should be able to play all of the content with your friends."
Specific details about multiplayer, like if you can run into other players in the open world like you can in Diablo 4's endgame, weren't mentioned. Blizzard said that information will have to wait until we're closer to its 2029 release.
One of the biggest changes that differentiates Diablo 5 from Diablo 4 is its return to having a procedurally-generated overworld and dungeons. This is supposed to convey the shifting nature of the world as you travel across the continent with your caravan cleansing it of Diablo's corruption. It's possible that this might dramatically change how you'll interact with other players once you're finished with the campaign, especially if everyone experiences their own version of Sanctuary.
Running into a bunch of other players might ruin the illusion that you're a lone hero fighting back against the forces of Hell. Blizzard says Diablo 5 will incorporate a lot of things it learned from Diablo 4, but it's unclear if that will include things like world events and bosses. Diablo 4 is also overflowing with skins and cosmetics that, if carried forward, would suggest there must be some way of showing off your fit to the other heroes of Sanctuary.
It doesn't seem like we're going to get any concrete answers about this for a while, though. Next year, Blizzard will start to post regular updates about the game's development to see how fans feel about it. Maybe one of them will shed some light on the scope of multiplayer in Diablo 5 and whether or not it'll continue what Diablo 4 started.

title: World of Warcraft: Forever devs say a direct sequel like Guild Wars 2 is unlikely: 'Why would you throw that away and start over?'
text:
World of Warcraft: Forever looks—well, pretty interesting, all told. Rather than just being a Season of Discovery-style reimagining of Classic, Forever promises to be a full-on remake of classic-era WoW. Reimagined class trees, new raids, and $30 elves . Don't think about the $30 elves too hard.
But it does beg the question, why is Blizzard doing this rather than, say, developing WoW 2? It worked out swimmingly for ArenaNet's Guild Wars series, after all. Speaking to IGN , Forever's principal designer Kris Zierhut says: "I think one of the things that's singularly great about WoW is we have this game and this world and this design that has been continuously developed for the last 25 years.
"And we keep making it better. We made the graphics better, we made the rendering better, we made the lighting better; all that new stuff we showed on stage today."
That is, in fairness, true—and true of retail, as well. Part of the reason why Classic works as a concept is because modern WoW is almost straight-up a different game—new models, animations, completely reimagined class designs, and a visual aesthetic that still holds up. Forever looks to be taking full advantage of retail's steady march of progress.
Zierhut says as much: "We've also made the way the engine draws things move more efficiently. The way the server runs, handling players and moving them around, and all the things that handle spells and combat, all of that's been made more efficient and better over the years. We have this incredible engine and server infrastructure driving the game that is second to none. Why would you throw that away and start over?"
I maintain that a WoW 2 wouldn't be superfluous. With all of that progress comes a lot of technical debt (see: player housing getting borked by fixing an elevator in a 13-year old raid), as well as a ton of design choices. A direct sequel's a chance to start over and challenge basic assumptions about the game's design—the Guild Wars series becoming an increasingly action-focused game , for instance.
There's also a second argument—and this, I feel more torn on—that Forever is trying to re-capture an outdated design. On the one hand, the cynic in me understands that modern MMOs are a hell of a lot different for good reason. We datamine new information about new patches weeks ahead of when they come out, we optimise everything down to the last, minute detail. We hug these games so hard that we wring all mystery out of them .
On the other hand, there has been a yearning, a rumbling. Our own Lincoln Carpenter said as much in our MMO column : "It's hard to argue that the MMOs of today aren't better designed than their older iterations. And yet, it's the moments when I step off the treadmill where they still feel the most magical." If Forever offers an alt-history not just of WoW, but of modern MMO design in general? Then I'm on board.

title: We tested the simple Windows 11 account bypass and it works. Just no-one tell Microsoft
text:
For security reasons, a Microsoft account is required to set up a fresh installation of Windows 11—unless you exploit this one weird oversight.
After navigating through the usual setup screens for a fresh installation of Windows 11 Home and connecting to the internet, Windows Latest reports that you'll want to keep your eyes peeled for the 'Let’s add your Microsoft account' screen. Apparently, clicking on the small 'learn more' link in the paragraph about sign-in options (and not 'learn more' next to the big blue 'Next' button) allows you to bypass the usual requirement for a Microsoft account.
If the bypass works as it has for us, the user skips ahead to the 'Who's going to use this device?' screen and is able to create a local account. After entering a password and setting three security questions, you can apparently use Windows via just the local account.
This Microsoft account bypass was first found by @TheBobPony on X . Windows Latest then tested it using an installation on a virtual machine and, to date, has only found the bypass in Windows Insider preview builds. Windows Latest notes that it's currently unclear which other versions of Windows 11 may also be affected. We tested the process as detailed by Windows Latest on a fresh installation of a non-Insider Preview build of Windows 11, and were able to replicate the bypass.
It's particularly interesting, given that the option for local account creation seemed to have been scrubbed from the normal Windows installation method long ago. Instead, you usually have to open a terminal and type a command to get Windows to reboot into an offline-only mode to bypass Microsoft account creation/sign in.
A new method for skipping the mandatory Microsoft Account login in Windows 11 Home Edition has been discovered... just simply click on the small Learn more hyperlink on the Microsoft Account login page. pic.twitter.com/Z91D65UW24 September 12, 2026
This doesn't, however, necessarily mean an officially supported local account option is in the works. For one thing, Microsoft has been working to make it harder to install Windows without an internet connection and a Microsoft account for some time now, and last year disabled the aforementioned popular 'bypassnro' Windows 11 sign-in workaround for Insider builds .
That said, even higher-ups at Microsoft don't love the account sign-in requirement. Vice president Scott Hanselman has previously said on X that he hates it , and that he's "working on it". Furthermore, Microsoft just had its biggest-ever Patch Tuesday— of the nearly 1,000 security flaws addressed , it feels odd that this relatively simple bypass has been overlooked.
Despite Windows and Devices VP Pavan Davuluri saying he wants Windows to be better, there's otherwise been little official movement on this particular point . For all intents and purposes, this bypass seems to be a bug, and not a feature.

title: Talent calculators have already been assembled for World of Warcraft: Forever, and there's some real interesting stuff in here
text:
World of Warcraft has a long-standing tradition of datamining and min-maxing. So it should come as no surprise that, despite only just being shown at Blizzcon, World of Warcraft: Forever now already has online talent calculators available, assembled from a delightful tapestry of streams and ravenous info-gatherers.
There's the old reliable that is WoWHead , but I want to shout out Reddit user Baldwinbuilds for their version , which not only collects all of the currently-known info about the Classic revamp's talents, but also has a handy button that tells you exactly how they were changed. It's a tremendous bit of work.
I've had a skim through, and assembled a list of some of the wildest additions—now, keep in mind, WoW Forever's not coming until November, so all of these are likely to change between now and its debut. But it still gives you an idea of the sorts of design philosophies that Blizzard's gearing up to apply:
Arms warriors get a new ability called Searing Strike, which does an 80% extra damage against Giants, Dragonkin, and mounted targets—knocking them off their steed to boot.
Retribution paladins have an interesting talent called Holy Twist. This debuffs an enemy whenever you replace your current seal on them with an echo, which then re-triggers it on your next melee attack. Basically, you'll be cycling through your seals.
Survival hunters seem to be dual wielders now with Predator's Edge, which increases your offhand damage by 10% per point, along with a bunch of new abilities that make your Mongoose Bite more effective.
Combat rogues borrow some tricks from retail's outlaw with Relentless Blades, which reduces their cooldowns whenever they use a finisher. This is a pretty big change, given it changes the flow of combat rogues completely.
Shamans get Totemic Projection, a huge quality of life buff, letting them take their totems with them on the move—as well as Call of the Elements, which lets you drop a full set of totems in one cast.
Other than that, it's a lot of popular snags from retail. Mages, for instance, get talents like Hot Streak, Arcane Blast, and Ice Lance, destruction warlocks get immolation, restoration shamans get Water Shield and druid healers get Wild Growth, and so on. Honestly, while it's early days, I'm surprised Blizzard hasn't gotten weirder.
But the Blizzcon demos only went up to level 38, and these are by no means finished. Searing Strike, in particular, feels like a stand-out to me, given how weirdly niche it is. And given how Blizzard's already bragged about Forever's unique, hyper-specific gear items, I'm looking forward to seeing how the studio experiments.

title: Thief designer Randy Smith Evergreen refused to work for Xbox because it would be like 'walking past some stakes with human skulls on them' and pretending 'it's probably fine in this direction'
text:
Randy Smith Evergreen had been pitching the idea to publishers for a while. A nonviolent RPG, in tune with the values of the Looking Glass games he worked on in the '90s, about a young American woman searching for her missing uncle in Eastern Europe. But the publishers weren't biting. Often, they'd tell Smith Evergreen how much they loved the Thief games he'd helped create, and he'd wonder whether he ought to just be pitching a spiritual sequel to that seminal stealth series instead. Then, Microsoft came calling.
"I had an opportunity to work for a studio that's funded by Xbox, and this was at the lowest moment of our funding search when we were like, 'This might not happen, we might need to think about how to feed our families in some other way,'" he recalls. "I held on—and ultimately it worked out, and I got a funded project—in part because I felt hesitancy to work for a Microsoft-backed studio. I think the recent layoffs at Microsoft showed that there was some wisdom to that decision."
(Image credit: Eidos Montreal) I ask Smith Evergreen where that hesitance came from—positing that it might have something to do with the fact that, over the decades, Microsoft's track record for keeping its studios open has been terrible. "You just answered your own question," he says.
For Xbox to buy them and quickly turn around in a few short years and dissolve the studio was just a pretty dire warning.
Randy Smith Evergreen
By the time Smith Evergreen had to make a decision about whether or not to join Xbox, the company had already shut down Arkane Austin—the Dishonored and Prey studio that, more than any other, had stuck fast to the design principles, worldbuilding and atmosphere of the Thief series.
"I have countless friends who worked there or were the founders of that studio, and I know the high quality work that they're capable of. And I know the tortured history of their last project, Redfall, and that its shortcomings weren't entirely attributable to the talent in that studio," Smith Evergreen says. "For Xbox to buy them and quickly turn around in a few short years and dissolve the studio was just a pretty dire warning. To take a job with them at that point would be like walking past some stakes with human skulls on them and being like, 'It's probably fine in this direction'. And I did consider it, but I'm glad I ultimately went a different way."
(Image credit: Bethesda Softworks) Smith Evergreen has "snatched success out of the jaws of defeat", starting a new indie studio to work on an unannounced game that evolved out of the original nonviolent RPG pitch. "It's quite different [from] that, but some of the mechanics of that larger indie RPG were prototyped, and I took what I thought would be most commercially successful and reduced its scope and changed quite a few other things as well," he says. "And that was the new pitch that ultimately got accepted. With some additional modifications that were proposed by the party who ultimately funded us."
Smith Evergreen's team jumped through a lot of hoops in order to loosen those purse-strings. "But where it is today is great," he says. "In our case, it did not torture the concept out of desirability. It's still a great game that we're excited to work on."
A common trait among game developers is that they thrive under limitations. Many of the medium's innovators have found ways to squeeze magic through a tight funnel of technical and financial constraint, all while navigating the demands of their paymasters. But Smith Evergreen points out that not all interference is welcome or productive.
(Image credit: Square Enix) "There have definitely been places in my past where I have felt unwanted pressure from people who are backing the game," he says. "I think a notable version would be the Thief series, especially Thief: Deadly Shadows, where Eidos pushed us to make the game a little bit more violent than we were interested in. And you can debate whether that's good feedback or not.
"My own inclinations might have been to rely so heavily on stealth when I was working on the Thief series that it wasn't accessible to a larger market, and their feedback maybe made it more accessible. But at the same time, I think there was a little bit of, at that time, Eidos wresting some creative control away from us."
It was Eidos who decided the game should be given the slightly daft and bloodythirsty subtitle of Deadly Shadows. "They didn't want to call it Thief 3, and they did want to emphasise murder," Smith Evergreen says. "The team wasn't stoked about that."
(Image credit: Ion Storm) Thief: Deadly Shadows was a AAA game at the time of its release in 2004. But since then, the costs involved in making a AAA game that meets modern standards have increased exponentially. So much so that Smith Evergreen believes the immersive sim genre no longer belongs in big-budget development.
"I think that might be a misread for the audience size of immersive sims," he says. "It's hard to know how an immersive sim wins the arms race to be AAA. And so there's quite a few of us who think the way to do it is to be triple-I or double-A. You're talking about a three to $10 million budget, a passionate team led by some of us folks who have experience with immersive sims or newcomers who just played a lot of immersive sims and really get it, making something that's a little bit smaller, more passionate, and can be made more quickly."
The original Thief cost $3 million to make, Smith Evergreen points out. "If you did it today, it'd be cheaper because the engine already exists, and you can get a lot of the functionality you need by just buying it off the shelf in the asset store. It's not clear to me that the $3 million dollar Thief or Deus Ex-style immersive sim that you want to make in the year 2026 is going to sell disproportionately different amounts of copies than the $250 million one that comes out of a big studio."
(Image credit: Remedy Entertainment) There's only so much fidelity a game needs, Smith Evergreen suggests. "I remember back when Alan Wake came out I was like, 'OK, this is relatively photoreal. I know 100% that I'm on a ferry. I see that I'm going to an island in the Pacific Northwest. Why do we need more graphics?' Because they just cost a ton."
Why do we need more graphics?
Randy Smith Evergreen
So long as the graphics are good enough to establish an imsim's vibe, says Smith Evergreen, that's enough. "Would fans prefer an immersive sim that's got insane spectacle and gorgeous, Arkane Lyon quality vistas? Of course they would like that. But is it necessary for what you come to an immersive sim for? I'm not as sure that it is."
Smith Evergreen is not the only respected game director I've interviewed recently who has struggled to get a new game off the ground. Dragon Age's David Gaider is fighting to fund a heist game. And Wyrdsong , the new RPG from Fallout 76 lead Jeff Gardiner, appears to have suffered death by a thousand cuts during the publisher pitching process.
(Image credit: Subset Games) The games market has been flooded with content. As a consequence, Smith Evergreen says, "There are games that people work on that just never get touched." Venture capitalists hunt for AI-driven projects and games-as-a-service to throw their money behind, while indies jostle to break through with dazzling new ideas.
"It's kind of like the same evolutionary path that the dinosaurs went through after the asteroid hit the Earth," Smith Evergreen says. "They went from an arms race to be bigger, to an arms race to be smaller. And if you think about it, a lot of the most beloved indie games of the past 30 years—FTL is one example—were cheap, fast, scrappy games that just had amazing gameplay and great creativity. And that's the direction I think a lot of things need to go right now, especially in the indie space. They need to be high quality content, but not enormous production budgets."
Meanwhile, Thief is going through something of a belated renaissance. A Nightdive-enabled remaster of The Dark Project is coming , alongside a graphic novel set between the first two games in the series. "I used to say that when I played Dishonored, that was the first time I ever played a Thief game," Smith Evergreen says. "Because when you make a game, it's just a totally different experience than having played it. But I feel like enough time has passed since I played Thief: The Dark Project that playing a remaster will probably feel very fresh for me. So I'm excited about that."
(Image credit: Nightdive) If Smith Evergreen were ever to be tempted back to the Thief series in the future, it would be to work on a low-budget entry that bypassed "spending infinite amounts of time on fancy art and rendering problems".
"I would not be super excited to work on a huge budget immersive sim Thief reboot," he says. "Working on these giant budget games, there's a little bit of torture to it. It takes a very long time. It's a messy process, especially for immersive sims—it can be very hard to find their centre before the moment when you need to build tonnes of content. There are just all these reasons that, as a creator, it's a challenging thing. And challenges are awesome, but not all challenges are equally fun."

title: Overwatch's newest hero is yet another example of how Team 4 is on a generational run
text:
The last time an Overwatch hero captured my heart like this, I ended up maining an old sniper for almost a decade, so I think I'll be seeing a hell of a lot of Overwatch's newest hero: Doctrine.
Unveiled at Blizzcon over the weekend, Doctrine is the newest addition to the Support roster (alongside Sombra), but he's unlike anything we've seen before. He's got some usual mechanics like a shift similar to Moira or Anran's—with a Sandevistan twist—a primary fire that can heal and damage, and an AOE ultimate which heals allies and reduces the health capacity of enemies. That's all standard stuff, and not particularly exciting—the juice of Doctrine's build comes from his second ability and right click.
Doctrine's second ability, Invigorating Drones, attaches to an ally and boosts their attack speed and healing. It is a nasty ability to tag onto a hitscan hero like Soldier: 76, Sojourn, or Sierra, especially if a Kiriko ult is in the mix.
As a support main, I'm always looking to support my team in more ways than just healing (although that should always be the priority), and helping teammates with an attack boost is something I didn't know I needed. I had so much fun over the weekend treating all DPS heroes as if they were pawns who I could buff just at the right time to instigate some impressive enemy team wipes. But even this isn't the star of Doctrine's kit.
The real hero is his right click, Infuse. This adds powerful effects onto whatever piece of kit he uses next:
He moves faster when shifting and has vertical reach with the added benefit of Fly.
Invigorating Drones can be used on himself buffing his attack speed and passive healing.
Primary fire changes to a charged hit which deals more healing and damage.
It doesn't seem like a lot, but this one mechanic raises up Doctrine's skill ceiling dramatically by giving him so many options to support his team in both healing and damage and provide great engagement and disengagement possibilities.
Doctrine is testimony to just how creative and innovative Team 4 continues to be. Since the rework earlier this year, they've been on something of a generational run when it comes to its new heroes. Each one has felt exciting in new ways, and offers up different approaches to the FPS, but Doctrine is the best I've seen so far.
